findings.title: Urgent requests for stale reports sharing one physical worker overwrite the outstanding assignment and strand training.
findings.description: A reused worker can own several retained simulated-time reports. The urgent loop sends requests for all of them concurrently, but _session_assignments permits only one current logical assignment per sid. Each request overwrites the preceding assignment and appends the same sid to training_sids. The first valid requested report is then rejected. Completing the last request removes the sole assignment but leaves the earlier client marked update_requested with a duplicate sid reservation, so aggregation waits indefinitely.
findings.reachability: Independent probe constructs the retained reports through actual _select_clients batching and actual report/chunk/part/completion handlers, starting with clean assignments. With asynchronous=True, simulate_wall_time=True, request_update=True, max_concurrency=1, clients_per_round=3, minimum_clients=1 and staleness_bound=1, one worker reports clients 7,2,9 in round 1. Client 9 reports again in rounds 2 and 3, while clients 7 and 2 retain future finish times 100 and 101. At round 3 the default should_request_update rule requests both old clients from that same worker. No synthetic retained queue or forced staleness predicate is used. The shipped PORT config enables the corresponding combination and max_concurrency=5 with per_round=30.

reproduction.first_requested_response: ValueError: Session does not match a current logical client assignment.
reproduction.stubs: Physical payload sends deliver the reports through real ingress handlers. Aggregation and wrap-up are inert; client selection, batching, retained queues, simulated-time advance, default staleness predicate, urgent dispatch, assignment checks and last-response completion execute.
reproduction.root_probe_boundary: Root synthetic-queue probe requests 7 then 2 and observes the same overwrite. Independent actual-batching probe requests 2 then 7, confirming that failure does not depend on request order.

findings.required_correction: Keep at most one outstanding urgent logical assignment per physical sid. Serialize or queue other urgent requests for that worker, preserve their report/byte accounting, and issue the next after the preceding response completes or cleanup releases it. Avoid duplicate training_sids. Preserve concurrent urgency for distinct workers, valid requested-response identities and rejection of wrong/stale sessions. Add a bounded reused-worker regression that finishes all requested responses and verifies round progress. No authentication, nonces or protocol redesign is required.
findings.test_gap: The all-buffered-stale regression uses distinct sids, and the existing reused-worker urgent test has only one urgent client. They do not cover multiple retained logical clients on one worker.
findings.baseline_boundary: The newly enforced single-current-assignment contract makes the previously concurrent same-worker urgent dispatch reject a response it just requested. This is a candidate-local interaction defect.

findings.title: Removing selected urgent reports corrupts the finish-time heap.
findings.description: reported_clients is maintained with heapq, but list.remove() does not restore its heap invariant. When only some buffered reports require urgency, later heappush/heappop can select a later-finishing client ahead of an earlier one, or move simulated wall_time backward. Snapshot iteration fixes skipped requests but does not preserve the chronological selection contract.

reproduction.setup: Actual _process_clients and report/chunk/part/completion handlers. Valid initial heap finish times [9,20,58,31,28,94]; round 20, wall_time 1, staleness_bound 10. Only client 20 starts at round 1; the others start at round 20. The default should_request_update selects client 20. Its actual urgent response has update_response=True and finish near 1.
reproduction.stubs: Socket emit plus downstream aggregate/wrap/select are inert. Urgency decision, heap removal, re-registration of the urgent assignment, actual ingress and selection of updates execute.

findings.required_correction: Restore the heap invariant after selective removal, before any concurrent response or subsequent heappush/heappop can use it. Keep snapshot enumeration. Add a partial-urgency regression that checks the selected client set/order and simulated-time progress, not only that all urgent requests were emitted.
findings.test_gap: The new all-buffered-stale test removes every entry and therefore cannot detect a corrupted remaining heap.
findings.baseline_boundary: The baseline indexed deletion also violated this invariant. This is a concrete latent defect in the revised, in-scope urgent path, not a claim that Phase 2B introduced the original ordering bug.

findings.title: Logical-client deduplication omits a distinct retained completed transfer.
findings.description: Queued wire accounting is keyed only by logical client ID. Every completed transfer carrying that ID is excluded when one queued entry exists, even when older completion-hook fields on another physical worker retain a different decoded report/payload. This undercounts retained buffers during normal asynchronous worker reassignment and permits ingress beyond max_buffered_bytes.

reproduction.setup: Three registered physical workers; asynchronous clients_per_round=3; third worker still trains logical client 3. First and second workers complete logical clients 1 and 7 through actual handlers, then processed queued accounting is released while legacy completion fields remain. Actual _select_clients chooses replacements [7,8]. While its first send awaits, the first worker completes the new logical client 7 before the second worker is reassigned.
reproduction.expected: Both distinct retained transfers count once. The third worker report must be rejected before parsing because 380+169 exceeds 400, without modifying its prior assignment or other workers.
reproduction.stubs: Payload sends are instrumented to deliver fast responses at the real await boundary; downstream report processing is inert. Actual assignment selection, completion hooks/ledger transition, report reservation and ingress execute.

findings.required_correction: Deduplicate the queued/completed references by transfer identity or owning session, rather than excluding all completed values with the same logical client ID. Retain legacy report/payload visibility and preserve queued bytes when the worker is reused. Verify the real selection await boundary, repeated logical identities across workers, processed release and disconnect/close cleanup.
findings.test_gap: The existing completed-unaggregated budget test covers one completion only; the reused-worker test uses different logical IDs on the same worker. Neither exercises distinct retained completions for a repeated logical ID.
findings.baseline_boundary: Introduced by the new Phase 2B buffer ledger.

optional_low_observations.title: Client socket/S3 paths do not apply max_buffered_bytes when it is below max_payload_bytes.
optional_low_observations.reproduction: DefaultPayloadStrategy accepts an 82-byte chunk with max_buffered_bytes=20 and max_payload_bytes=max_chunk_bytes=256 on both interpreters. InboundTransfer.reserve checks only the payload cap; client S3 uses the same reserve. Client simulated-file ingress applies min(payload, buffered).
optional_low_observations.impact_and_limit: Client ingress still has a finite payload cap. The evidence specifically describes the global buffer budget as a server ledger, so this narrower client configuration inconsistency is not a separate blocking acceptance failure.
optional_low_observations.optional_correction: Make the scope of max_buffered_bytes consistent and explicit. If it is shared with client ingress, apply it before retaining client socket/S3 bytes; otherwise document the server-only budget and the separate client payload cap.
